quote.text: Creditors have better memories than debtors.
quote.author: Benjamin Franklin, Poor Richard’s Almanack, 1758

stories.headline: Araghchi offers to reopen Hormuz in two days; Washington has not accepted
stories.dek: Oil fell anyway. Brent lost $9.49 on Monday, 8.4 per cent, to $103.96 — and the Hormuz strait stayed shut to everyone.

stories.headline: Amended filing puts Anthropic’s compute commitment at $895.4 billion to 2045
stories.dek: Monday’s amendment filled a blank the 26 October original left empty. Nine-month revenue was $33.2 billion; the box marked “Run-Rate Revenue as of October 31” is still empty.

stories.kicker: The Undercurrent · Benteng Bigas, Meron Na
stories.headline: The Philippines sells rice at twenty pesos and lifts the market price
stories.dek: Rice inflation reached 20.3 per cent in September, and 23.6 for the poorest third of households. A record 961,346 Filipinos queued for the twenty-peso ration.

stories.headline: Manpower ministry investigates about forty-five firms over Changi work passes
stories.dek: About 270 workers employed by SATS contractors may have been wrongly deployed, the ministry said on 2 November; it has told SATS to tighten oversight beneath it.

stories.headline: The twenty-year guarantee on a Gränsfors axe excludes its handle
stories.dek: A replacement handle is CAD $45 to $60 against CAD $230 for the axe; the part that fails is the wood.

stories.headline: XREAL opens Aura orders at $1,099 and publishes no battery life
stories.dek: Google calls it the first wired glasses running its headset system: 95 grams on the face, a 265-gram puck in the pocket, shipping mid-November. No Singapore price exists.

stories.headline: Sinn re-makes its Spacelab chronograph, 300 pieces at €5,490
stories.dek: Reinhard Furrer bought his own 140 S before the 1985 mission. Frankfurt’s 65th-anniversary version is 44mm, and its power reserve is published as both 42 and 46 hours.

stories.headline: My Chemical Romance reach their first No. 1, twenty years late
stories.dek: The Black Parade took 78,000 units, up 653 per cent, to top the Billboard 200 dated 7 November — the longest wait to a first No. 1 in the chart’s history.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · The Period Diary
stories.headline: O’Brien and Bonny log 506 cycles; period pain in 74 per cent
stories.dek: Published on 30 October in the Journal of Pediatric and Adolescent Gynecology: health, school and activities were each affected in about one cycle in five, and a four-item pain score predicted which.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Real Yield
stories.headline: Oil fell 8.4 per cent and Treasury real yields rose
stories.dek: The ten-year inflation breakeven narrowed again, 2.34 to 2.29 per cent, while the ten-year Treasury real yield rose two basis points to 2.62. Oil relief bought no easing at all.

stories.headline: Tokyo protects 786 stitched garments; 324 are Aomori work trousers
stories.dek: Pinterest searches for “sashiko ideas” rose 1,509 per cent this year. The stitching began because Edo-period Tsugaru farmers were forbidden to wear cotton.

stories.headline: The Attica cohort finds midlife starters level with the lifelong active
stories.dek: Published 19 October: odds of frailty after 22 years were 0.21 for the Attica adults who became active against 0.20 for the never-stopped — and 1.28, no benefit at all, for those who let it slide.

stories.kicker: The Diary · Two Deadlines This Month
stories.headline: National Gallery Singapore discounts Pop after Pop 30 per cent to 30 November
stories.dek: Tennis Australia’s early-bird pricing for the 2027 Open ends at 12:59pm on the same day, and Tokyo’s January sumo opens its advance sale on Saturday 5 December.
